steps: Halve the avocado, remove the stone, and scoop the flesh into a bowl
Mash with a fork to your preferred texture and stir in the lime juice and a pinch of salt
Finely dice the tomato and red onion, then fold through the mash with chopped coriander and finely diced jalapeño (seeds removed for less heat)
Taste and adjust the lime juice and salt
Serve immediately with the corn tortilla chips
Cook the rice and boil the eggs (about 8-9 minutes for a firm yolk), then cool both under cold running water
Boil or steam the edamame in the pod for 3-4 minutes, drain, and season lightly with salt
Cut the cucumber into sticks and peel and halve the eggs
Divide the rice, egg, edamame, and cucumber sticks evenly between airtight containers
Drizzle each box with tamari just before eating
Toss the warm rice with sesame oil and a pinch of salt
Beat the egg and cook it into a thin sheet in a lightly oiled pan, then slice into strips
Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry, and season with a little sesame oil and salt; cut the carrot into matchsticks and sauté briefly until just tender
Lay a nori sheet shiny-side down on a bamboo mat and spread a thin, even layer of rice over it, leaving a 2cm strip bare at the top edge
Arrange lines of carrot, spinach, pickled radish, and egg strip across the rice, then roll tightly from the bottom using the mat, sealing the bare edge with a dab of water
Slice each roll into bite-sized pieces with a sharp, damp knife
Warm the mandazi in a low oven or dry pan for a few minutes if you prefer them hot
Slice the banana
Serve each portion with two pieces of mandazi alongside the sliced banana
Blend the frozen açaí purée with a splash of water or milk until thick and smooth, pulsing to break up the frozen block
Slice the banana
Pour the açaí base into a bowl
Top with the granola and banana slices, then drizzle with agave
Combine the cooked rice, coconut milk, and a pinch of ground cardamom in a saucepan
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often
Reduce the heat and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring regularly, until thickened and creamy
Stir in the maple syrup and remove from the heat
Divide between bowls and top with the diced mango
Warm the cooked rice with the milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring until it loosens into a soft porridge, about 5 minutes
Divide the warm rice porridge between bowls
Top each with a spoonful of skyr, a drizzle of honey, and a scattering of mixed berries
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and line a baking tray
Divide the sausage meat into 4 portions and flatten each into a thin patty on a sheet of cling film
Place a peeled hard-boiled egg in the centre of each patty and use the cling film to help wrap the meat evenly around the egg, sealing the edges
Roll each wrapped egg in the almond flour to coat
Arrange on the tray and bake for 20-25 minutes, turning once, until the sausage is golden and cooked through
Cool slightly before halving or serving whole
Partially freeze the beef for about 30 minutes to firm it up, then slice thinly (around 3mm) against the grain
Toss the strips with the coconut aminos, salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika, massaging to coat evenly
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight for deeper flavour
Shake off excess marinade and lay the strips in a single layer on dehydrator trays, leaving space between pieces
Dehydrate at 60-65°C (145°F) for about 4 hours, checking from 3 hours, until firm, dry, and bendable without snapping
Cool completely before storing in an airtight container
Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl
Scatter the granola over the top
Add the mixed berries
Serve straightaway so the granola stays crisp
Spoon a third of the soy yogurt into a glass or bowl
Layer with a portion of the granola, berries, and walnuts
Repeat the layers with the remaining yogurt, granola, berries, and walnuts
Serve immediately
Toast the waffles according to the packet instructions until golden and crisp
Plate the waffles and top with a dollop of Greek yogurt
Drizzle over the maple syrup and serve warm
Whisk the chia seeds into the oat milk with the maple syrup until well combined
Divide between 4 jars or small containers
Stir each again after 10 minutes to stop the chia clumping, then cover and refrigerate overnight
Before serving, stir to loosen and top with the berries
Mash the banana in a bowl or jug
Stir in the oats, oat milk, chia seeds, and maple syrup until combined
Divide the mixture between jars
Cover and refrigerate overnight until thickened
Stir well before eating, loosening with a splash more oat milk if needed
